statusText:
The CME weekend halt still defines the entire horizon. NQ has not quoted since Friday's 21:00 UTC weekly close and will not quote again until roughly 22:00 UTC on Sunday 16 August, about ninety minutes beyond the end of this 24-hour window. Tail is 12% (low), the action is EA_ON and the status is green, because a pathological one-way price path cannot form while no venue is quoting.

This hour added confirmation rather than escalation, which is why the scores are held rather than moved. Independent reporting now pins the southern Lebanon strikes at Ansar and Deir al-Zahrani - roughly 18 km apart - with 11 dead in the lower counts and 15 in the higher ones, including three children, and 12 or more wounded, making it one of the deadliest days since the June truce. Israel's military frames both sites as Hezbollah infrastructure on and around the Ali al-Taher ridge; Hezbollah says the attacks will be 'met with what they deserve'. The material new detail is procedural: the US-brokered track has been stalled since the Rome round ended without agreement on 6 August, divided over the Israeli withdrawal timetable, and Netanyahu's spokesman is now asking for 'more serious' talks while President Aoun reads the strike as a message aimed at the negotiating process itself. A stalled track plus a promised retaliation is a harder configuration to defuse over a weekend than a single one-sided strike, so Stress holds at 67% (high) rather than easing.

The Hormuz backdrop is unchanged and still heavy: shipping through the strait is running near 17% of the pre-conflict average with roughly 151 transits in the past seven days, 56 reports of vessel damage since the war began on 28 February, and Washington preparing further economic measures while Tehran refuses to concede control. Every hard mark was re-verified this hour and every one is Friday's: NQ futures 30,141.75 (-0.15%, session range 30,028.50-30,283.00), VIX 14.25 (-2.60%, range 14.18-14.72), WTI $82.40 (+1.42%) and Brent $88.52 (+1.67%), with the Fed's own H.15 release showing 2-year 4.15% and 10-year 4.63% on its 13 August observation. A 14-handle VIX sitting against that geopolitical tape remains the central unresolved divergence, and it gets resolved at the reopen, not before.
recommendation: Base strategies stay enabled: Tail 12% maps to EA_ON. There is nothing to trade into and nothing to protect against while the venue is closed - existing-position management, exits and emergency protection remain active as always. Treat Sunday's roughly 22:00 UTC restart as the single checkpoint that matters: it is the first opportunity for a full weekend of two-sided Middle East headlines, a promised Hezbollah retaliation, a stalled Rome track and a prepared US economic-isolation package to be priced at once in a thin auction, and it anchors the danger window rather than any point inside this horizon. This is general market-state analysis for a public dashboard, not personalised financial advice.
headline: Weekend halt holds Tail at 12% and status green; Lebanon strikes confirmed at 11-15 dead with the Rome track stalled since 6 August, so Stress stays 67% into Sunday's 22:00 UTC restart
body:
Price path: none exists. The entire 24-hour horizon sits inside the CME weekend halt, so there is no session direction, no gap, no retracement structure, no failed pullback and no proximity to extremes to score. Every price input is a Friday close carried forward, which is both the correct reason for Tail to be low and the correct reason for Confidence to sit at 66% (solid) rather than higher.

Friday's marks, all re-verified against primary sources this hour: NQ futures settled 30,141.75, down 46.75 points or 0.15%, having traded 30,028.50 to 30,283.00 on 397,964 contracts - a narrow, unremarkable range with no directional efficiency worth scoring. VIX closed 14.25, down 2.60%, with a 14.18-14.72 range. WTI settled $82.40 (+1.42%) and Brent $88.52 (+1.67%), both firmer on the week as talks to end the Iran war stayed stalled. The Fed's H.15 release gives 2-year 4.15% and 10-year 4.63% at the 13 August observation. Nothing in that cross-asset set is aligned into a one-way structure; if anything it conflicts, and conflicting signals belong in Stress, not Tail.

Geopolitics is the only live variable and it moved sideways this hour. The Lebanon strikes are now corroborated across multiple outlets with a casualty range of 11 to 15 and three children among the dead. Hezbollah has promised a response. Israel has asked for 'more serious' US-brokered talks. Lebanon's prime minister rejected the claim that the dead were military targets and insisted weapons management on Lebanese soil is the state's exclusive responsibility. The Rome round collapsed on 6 August over withdrawal timelines and has not resumed. Separately, Hormuz remains the structural energy risk: transit volumes near 17% of normal, 56 vessel-damage reports since 28 February, Trump repeating a threat to declare the strait US territory and Iran vowing to retain control. None of this is priced, because nothing is trading.

Why Tail stays at 12% and not higher: Tail measures a pathological price path, not the size of a pending headline stack. There is no path. The full amplifier checklist - persistent directional efficiency, shallow pullbacks, repeated extension after failed retracements, NQ pinned near an extreme, aligned yields, VIX, oil, semis, megacaps and breadth - is unobservable and will stay unobservable for another twenty-three and a half hours. Publishing an elevated Tail now would assert structure that no venue has produced.

Why Stress stays at 67% and does not decay: the weekend has accumulated a two-sided Lebanon exchange with an explicit retaliation threat, a negotiating track stalled for nine days, an ongoing Hormuz blockade, further US economic measures in preparation, and a 14-handle VIX that has priced none of it. That backlog does not shrink while the market is shut - it compounds. The single checkpoint that matters is the roughly 22:00 UTC Sunday CME restart, when a thin opening auction takes the whole weekend at once. That is where the danger window sits, and it is one hour beyond the far edge of this forecast horizon.

Confidence at 66% (solid) reflects an honest split: the macro calendar, index, volatility, energy and rate marks are all verified against primary sources this hour and are internally consistent, but the single most informative input for this strategy - live price path - is structurally unavailable until Sunday night.

lookbackSummary: The trailing 24 hours are almost entirely post-close. Claude published every hour from 22:00 UTC Friday through 21:00 UTC Saturday. Tail never left the low band, running 2% in the first hours after the weekly close, settling at 9-10% through the Saturday European and US sessions and easing up to 12% by 21:00 UTC. Stress is the variable that actually moved: 12-14% immediately after the close, jumping to 45-46% once the weekend geopolitical picture was re-scored, then climbing monotonically through the Saturday news cycle - 48%, 50%, 53%, 55%, 58%, 60%, 62%, 65% - to 67% as the Lebanon strikes turned into a confirmed two-way exchange. Confidence rebuilt in parallel from 36-38% to 66% as primary-source marks were re-verified. Action was EA_ON and status green for all 24 hours, and dominantMode was mixed for all but the first two.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours end at 21:00 UTC Sunday, roughly one hour before the CME restart, so the entire forecast window stays inside the halt. Tail is therefore held in the low band throughout, drifting only from 12% to 14% as the reopen approaches and pre-auction positioning risk becomes non-trivial - EA_ON and green for all 24 slots. Stress grinds from 67% to 72% because unpriced weekend headline risk compounds rather than decays while the venue is shut: a promised Hezbollah retaliation, a Rome track stalled since 6 August, an ongoing Hormuz blockade and a prepared US economic package all remain outstanding. Confidence eases from 66% to 62% as Friday's marks age past 70 hours with nothing newer to test them. The last two slots switch to event/whipsaw to reflect a thin opening auction that has to absorb the whole weekend at once.

forecastDetail.comment: Saturday 22:00-23:00 UTC sits deep inside the CME weekend halt. No venue is quoting NQ, so no pathological price path can form and Tail stays at 12% with EA_ON. Stress holds at 67% because the Lebanon exchange is now two-sided and the Rome track has been stalled since 6 August.

Overnight European Saturday. Headline flow thins but does not stop; the risk this hour is a Hezbollah retaliation claim or an Israeli follow-up wave landing with no market able to price it. Tail unchanged, Stress unchanged.
Deepest part of the weekend news lull. Nothing scheduled, no macro, no venue. Scores held flat deliberately - drift here would be noise, not information.

Sunday pre-dawn UTC. Middle East morning begins; Israeli overnight operations and Lebanese casualty updates typically surface in this band. Still no price discovery, so any escalation accumulates as unpriced Stress rather than Tail.

Sunday Middle East daytime. Stress steps to 68% to reflect a full extra day of two-way Lebanon risk plus 56 vessel-damage reports in and around Hormuz accumulating with no market open to absorb them. Tail stays 12% - the halt still forbids a one-way path.
Sunday morning Europe. Confidence drifts to 64% as Friday's marks - NQ 30,141.75, VIX 14.25, WTI $82.40 - age past 60 hours with nothing newer to test them against.
